task.title: HealthKit corrections + Cardio-readiness implementation (Parts A-F), both candidates reviewed

result.summary: Claude implemented, tested, and had independently fresh-context reviewed (APPROVE on both) all six parts (A-F) of the corrections-and-Cardio-readiness task: Native Activity cache/read consistency; Server Strength telemetry presentation ownership; a new atomic workout-policy family-scope-replacement mechanism; a new bounded deferred-Cardio-observation reconciliation runner; canonical-workout-aware whole-day Activity attribution wiring; and a decision that Activity Detail (not a new Log row) is the right visible surface for Cardio. Code/test/review only, exactly as authorized. Neither final candidate has been pushed, deployed, uploaded, or activated. Production and the installed Native build are unchanged.

tests.summary: Combined directly-affected Server tests 214/214. Broader suites (package7, phase3, phase4, phase6, phase6.training, native-sandbox) all match the long-established pre-existing-failure baseline exactly, zero new failures. Native: 188/188 targeted, 1352/1353 full unit bundle (1 pre-existing unrelated bundle-version-literal failure). Mutation-tested 5 critical guards total (orchestrator + Server reviewer), all genuine RED-then-GREEN. Production webpack build passed repeatedly with explicitly captured exit code 0.

review.summary: Two independent fresh-context adversarial reviews: final Server candidate 01d1900b APPROVE (two minor non-blocking notes: copy-pasted helper functions across three new/touched runner files, a reused parameter name that is a readability nit only); final Native candidate 236f208e APPROVE (one accepted nuance: .reload can join an already-in-flight identical request rather than always issuing its own, which is still always live data, never stale).

zero_write_audit.summary: Parts C and D's new mutation-capable tooling (atomic policy replacement, deferred-Cardio reconciliation) has never been run against any real database or policy record -- tested exclusively against in-memory fixture stores. No production write of any kind occurred in this task.

decisions_required: Authorize Server deployment of 01d1900bcbb9db32ce270e49c7d24e919ba0d7d7 (ships the Part B/E presentation fixes and the Part C/D tooling capabilities -- activates nothing by itself).
Authorize Native release (archive, dry-run, then separately TestFlight upload) of 236f208edffddcad4ace8748874993ed7daa05da.
After both are live/installed and used normally: authorize a dry-run, then separately an apply, of the atomic workout-policy replacement (Strength-only -> [cardio, strength]).
After that: authorize a dry-run, then separately an apply, of the bounded reconciliation of the two specific already-deferred Sep24 Indoor Walk observations.
Strategic-eligibility changes remain explicitly out of scope for any of the above and need their own future separate authorization.
unexpected_findings: Part E required a genuine, non-mechanical product-judgment call (should an unconfirmed-candidate Strength workout's energy count toward whole-day totals, the way it now counts toward presentation?) -- decided NO for Strength (requires the same confirmed link Strength already uses to gate everything else) and unconditionally YES for Cardio (which structurally has no confirm/deny step at all, so canonicalization is its only inclusion decision); both fresh-context reviewers independently examined and accepted this reasoning as structurally forced, not arbitrary.

One implementation agent (Part E+F) hit a stream-watchdog stall mid-task after ~500 lines of real, uncommitted progress; resumed from that exact point (not restarted) to preserve its reasoning, and completed cleanly.

Disk space in the Server worktree got tight (as low as ~3.7GB free) across four sequential implementation passes each running a full production webpack build; managed by cleaning the regenerable .next output between parts -- no archive, worktree, or simulator data was ever at risk.

Independent Server reviewer found a real (non-blocking) DRY violation: three drift-fence/audit-row helper functions are copy-pasted verbatim across the pre-existing precedent runner and the two new Part C/D runners rather than factored into a shared module -- a future maintenance risk worth addressing before a fourth such runner is ever added.
backlog: Factor the copy-pasted digest/stable/listDigest helper functions (HealthKitWorkoutLinkReassessmentRunner.js, HealthKitActivationPolicyRunner.js, HealthKitDeferredWorkoutReconciliationRunner.js) into one shared module.
Consider tightening Part C's acknowledgeNarrowing from a bare boolean to requiring the caller to echo back the exact dropped-family list.

Server deploy -> Native release -> policy-replacement dry-run/apply -> deferred-Cardio-reconciliation dry-run/apply -> real-device acceptance, in that exact order, each with its own separate authorization (see decisions_required).
